commitResults.messageBody: Move command input and all user-facing messages out of Arin so its remaining responsibilities can be separated into Parser and TaskList in later increments. Add a focused Ui regression test while preserving the existing command output.

Add Command as the common execution contract and move the bye behaviour into ExitCommand. Arin now obtains the exit decision from the command, establishing the command-pattern seam for incrementally moving the remaining operations out of the main loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Jar: package application as executable fat JAR

commitResults.messageBody:
JavaDoc tags and method headers use inconsistent formatting, which makes the public API documentation harder to scan.

Standardize tags, convert short headers to multi-line Javadocs, use American spelling, and wrap the overlong error message.

Java code changes need a consistent project-specific standard to follow.

Add the SE-EDU Java coding-standard skill and require agents to load it
before Java code work.

Future commits need a shared convention for messages and branch names.

Add the SE-EDU Git-standard skill and require agents to load it before
proposing or creating commits.

Configure Gradle to run Checkstyle 11.0.0 against production and test sources.\n\nAdd rules based on the SE-EDU Java coding standard and suppressions for test Javadocs that are intentionally optional.

Configure Gradle with the JavaFX dependencies required by the tutorial.

Add the JavaFX Application and separate launcher classes so the project
can start the HelloWorld stage through ./gradlew run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task sorting by name and deadline
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks currently stay in insertion order, making it harder to scan a
long list alphabetically or identify the earliest deadlines.

Add sort name and sort deadline commands for the C-Sort extension.
Preserve task details and completion status, retain the order of ties,
and place tasks without deadlines after dated tasks. Save the new
order before updating in-memory positions so a failed save does not
silently renumber the user's tasks.

Reuse the command abstraction and numbered-list output to keep the
change focused. Document the console entry point, sorting rules, and
the effect of sorting on subsequent task-number commands.

Verify the change with 67 JUnit tests, including console integration
tests, both Checkstyle checks, and a Java 25 bundled JAR build.

The C-Sort extension has been developed and tested on codex/c-sort.
Bring it into master so users can order tasks by name or deadline
while preserving task details and consistent task numbers.

Keep the feature branch visible in history to record this extension
as a distinct increment. All 67 JUnit tests and both Checkstyle checks
pass, and the Java 25 bundled JAR builds successfully.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JavaFX for the build machine's architecture
commitResults.messageBody:
The bundled JAR contains Intel macOS libraries even when Gradle runs on
Apple Silicon. Launching it with a Java 25 runtime without JavaFX fails
because those libraries cannot load on ARM64.

Select the macOS JavaFX dependencies for the architecture of the Java
runtime running Gradle. Retain the Windows and Linux dependencies.

Bundle only one macOS architecture per JAR because the native library
filenames are shared between the Intel and Apple Silicon variants.
This lets the Apple Silicon build run without a separate JavaFX install.

Validation: rebuild the bundled JAR and confirm that it launches and
renders with a Java 25 runtime that contains no JavaFX modules.

The README explains IDE setup but does not explain how to package or
run the application with its JavaFX dependencies included.

Without packaging guidance, users can distribute the ordinary JAR and
encounter missing JavaFX dependencies on another computer.

Document the Shadow JAR build command, output path, Java 25 requirement,
launch command, and expected Hello World window. Explain the native
library coverage and the need to match the macOS build architecture.

Keep these instructions in the README so the build and distribution
workflow is available alongside the existing setup instructions.

Validation: check the commands and output against the successful JAR
build and launch using a Java 25 runtime without JavaFX modules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert validated task data during development
commitResults.messageBody:
Task constructors rely on the command parser to supply descriptions,
deadline dates, and event times that have already been validated.
Violating these assumptions can leave invalid state inside a task.

Document those internal contracts with Java assert statements and
diagnostic messages. Enable assertions for Gradle runs and tests, and
document the -ea flag for direct JAR launches.

Keep user-input validation in the command parser so ordinary input
errors still receive helpful messages even when assertions are disabled.
Add tests that verify assertion failures for invalid internal task data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task parsing from application flow
commitResults.messageBody:
Arin's main class coordinates commands and also contains all task
parsing rules. Long parsing branches and numeric separator offsets make
those rules harder to review and test independently. The UI also repeats
the numbered-list layout for ordinary lists and search results.

Extract task creation into TaskParser with a focused method per task
type and named separators. Delegate both list views to a shared display
helper, preserving their headings, numbering, and task order.

Keep command syntax, error messages, and storage representations intact
so the refactor improves readability without changing user behavior.
Add parser regression tests and retain the exact-output UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for task search and storage conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
Task searching and storage conversion each build a result list with an
explicit loop. Their intent is to filter matching tasks or map tasks to
storage lines, which Java streams can express directly.

Use a filter pipeline for case-insensitive search and a map pipeline
for task serialization. Preserve encounter order, duplicate entries,
and the existing storage format.

Collect search results into a separate mutable ArrayList to preserve
the previous behavior. Keep Locale.ROOT normalization so matching does
not depend on the computer's default locale.

Add regression tests for empty inputs, duplicates, result-list mutation,
locale-independent matching, and ordered storage output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match task assertions to parser whitespace rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Task parsing validates details with trim(), whereas isBlank() recognizes
additional Unicode whitespace. An assertion using isBlank() can reject
input that the parser accepts, turning a user command into an internal
assertion failure when development checks are enabled.

Use the same trim-based emptiness rule in task assertions as in the
parser. Add a Unicode em-space regression test to keep assertion-enabled
execution consistent with ordinary command validation.

Task constructors rely on validated descriptions, dates, and event times.

Integrate Java assertions for these internal contracts and enable them
for development runs and tests. Preserve ordinary validation behavior,
including the parser's existing Unicode whitespace rules.

Validation: all 23 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass with Java 25.
Malformed CLI commands still produce user-facing error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sync A-CodeQuality with the assertions increment
commitResults.messageBody:
Master now includes the merged assertions increment while the code
quality branch still starts from the earlier shared base.

Merge master into A-CodeQuality so the extracted parser is checked
against the task-data contracts before its pull request is merged.
Preserve both increments and their separate commit histories.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sync A-Streams with the assertions increment
commitResults.messageBody:
Master now includes task assertions, but the parallel streams branch
still starts from the earlier shared base.

Merge master into A-Streams so search and storage tests also run with
the internal task-data contracts enabled before integration.
Preserve the independently developed stream pipelines and their tests.

Task creation rules are mixed into the main loop, and task-list views
repeat their display logic.

Integrate the TaskParser extraction and shared numbered-list renderer
while preserving command syntax, error messages, and storage formats.
Sync the branch with the assertions increment before integration so
both changes are verified together.

Validation: all 42 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sync A-Streams with the code quality refactor
commitResults.messageBody:
Master now includes the extracted task parser and shared list renderer.
The streams branch must include that latest base before its final merge.

Merge master into A-Streams and preserve the search and serialization
pipelines alongside the refactored application flow. Verify the complete
test suite and style checks before merging the final increment.

Task search and storage conversion use explicit collection loops.

Integrate stream filtering and mapping while preserving task order,
duplicates, locale-independent matching, mutable search results, and
the existing storage format. Sync with both earlier increments before
merging so assertions, parsing, and streams are verified together.

Validation: all 47 JUnit tests, both Checkstyle tasks, the standalone
exit test, and the bundled JAR build and CLI smoke test pass on Java 25.

The documentation still contains the starter guide and does not explain
how to use Arin's task commands. Users also need clear warnings about
the placeholder GUI and the lack of automatic loading after a restart.

Replace the template with a Java 25 quick start, examples for every
command, expected results, a command summary, and troubleshooting.
Explain search-result numbering, sorting, and save-file limitations so
users can avoid changing the wrong task or overwriting an old record.

Add GitHub Pages metadata and link the guide from the project README.
Correct the obsolete entry-point path in the developer instructions.

Check the examples against the bundled JAR in an isolated directory,
including invalid inputs and restart behavior. Gradle tests, Checkstyle,
and the bundled JAR build pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge the published user guide into master
commitResults.messageBody:
The A-UserGuide task publishes the product guide from master's docs
folder. Integrate the guide developed on Published-UG so GitHub Pages
can serve it while retaining the requested documentation branch.

Keep the documented commands and limitations aligned with the tested
console application. No application behavior is changed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Arin's robot welcome window and screenshot
commitResults.messageBody:
The product website has no Ui.png, and the JavaFX window only shows a
Hello World label. The supplied robot illustration alone is not a
full-window screenshot as required by the course.

Bundle the unchanged illustration as a classpath resource and show it
in a titled Arin welcome window. Include console launch instructions
and clearly state that task commands still run outside the GUI.

Capture the running window, including its title bar, as docs/Ui.png.
Embed it in the guide, update the launch descriptions, and identify
the artwork as user-supplied without claiming original authorship.

Verify all 68 JUnit tests, both Checkstyle checks, and the Java 25 JAR
build. Check that the image is packaged, launches from another folder,
and appears without clipping in the captured window.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge the Arin screenshot into master
commitResults.messageBody:
The welcome window and its screenshot were developed on Published-UG.
Bring them into master so GitHub Pages publishes the current window
at Ui.png and displays it in the product guide.

Preserve the console-only task workflow and the existing A-UserGuide
tag. All 68 tests and Checkstyle checks pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore tasks and protect failed saves
commitResults.messageBody:
Saved tasks were never loaded, so the first change after restarting
could replace existing data with an incomplete list.

Load and validate every saved record before accepting changes. Preserve
the original file on malformed input, and require an atomic replacement
when saving. Keep in-memory tasks unchanged when a save fails.

Separate event time fields so free-text start and end values round-trip
without guessing. Explain how to repair legacy event records instead
of silently changing their meaning.

Share the command session between interfaces, handle end-of-input, and
cover restart, validation, corrupt files, and save failures with tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle JavaFX for both Mac architectures
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous JAR bundled only the build machine's Mac libraries.
Intel and Apple-silicon libraries have identical filenames, so simply
including both dependency sets would choose one arbitrarily.

Keep native binaries in platform-specific resource directories and
select the matching set before JavaFX starts. Include the JavaFX
classes for Windows, Linux, and macOS in the same fat JAR.

Check platform mappings and every indexed binary in regression tests.
Verify the packaged GUI with a Java 25 runtime without JavaFX to avoid
mistaking locally installed libraries for bundled dependencies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the Arin window an interactive task chat
commitResults.messageBody:
The welcome window required a separate console for task commands and
did not meet the final GUI requirement.

Connect a reusable FXML controller to the persistent command session.
Support Enter, Send, and Help, and keep messages readable when the
window is resized. Distinguish user messages, replies, and errors with
alignment, labels, and colors while retaining the supplied robot image.

Exercise the real controls, task commands, restart, and resizing with a
standalone GUI smoke test. Replace the product screenshot with a full
capture of this working interface.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the release across desktop platforms
commitResults.messageBody:
A build on one Mac cannot verify Windows, Linux, or Intel Mac loading.
Build one Java 25 fat JAR in CI and drive the actual GUI from empty
folders on all four supported platforms using that same artifact.

Run regression and style checks before producing the candidate. Keep
the test driver separate from the distributed JAR and limit workflow
permissions to read-only repository access.

Preserve complete wrapped messages at narrow widths and use grayscale
text smoothing to avoid colored edges on high-density Mac displays.

The published guide still described a welcome-only window and warned
that saved tasks would not be restored.

Explain the working chat controls, automatic restart loading, and safe
recovery of legacy event records. Point users to the release JAR and
document supported platforms, help, and data-file limitations.

Refresh the full-window screenshot and credit the tutorial and OpenJFX
design references. Keep the missing original artwork source explicit.
Provide a repeatable teammate and publication checklist without claiming
that human testing or historical course participation is verified.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge the final Arin release into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring the tested interactive GUI, safe restart persistence, and
cross-platform JavaFX bundle onto the published default branch.

Publish the matching User Guide, full-window screenshot, and release
checklist from master so the source, documentation, and release remain
consistent. Preserve all earlier increment tags and branch history.
